title: Differential eventstream replayer with heuristic conflict resolution
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Implement a differential replayer service and orchestration tooling that can reprocess only the delta (late-arriving or corrected) events for console usage analytics and telemetry, resolve ordering/duplicate conflicts heuristically, and produce idempotent outputs for downstream metrics and dashboards. The goal is to reduce cost and runtime of large backfills while preserving correctness for downstream consumers (billing, console metrics, and metric alerts). This ticket covers: design and implementation of a lightweight differ component, fuzzy deduplication strategy, conflict-resolution heuristics, checkpointing/resume tokens, rate-limited apply workers, and integration with existing backfill orchestration. The replayer should support dry-run mode, sampling-based validation, and automated sanity checks before commit.
acceptance_criteria: Replayer identifies delta set (late/updated events) for a given time window without scanning entire historical store
Conflict-resolution heuristics documented and implemented (last-write-wins with exponential confidence scoring + tombstone handling)
End-to-end run that replays a 7-day delta of 100M events completes with <10% cost of full reprocess and produces byte-for-byte stable outputs for sampled keys
Checkpoints are durable and resume-able; failed runs automatically resume from last checkpoint
Observability: per-run throughput/lag/cost dashboards and anomaly alerts are available in Console under project console-analytics-replay
Includes a rollback path and runbook for misapplied replays
comments: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting — agreed on differential approach instead of full snapshot replays to reduce egress/cost. Owners: Aisha (lead), Diego (implementation), Priya (observability)

2026-03-05: Spike results — small window delta extraction using event index + watermarking is ~4x faster than naive scan for typical customer load. Proof-of-concept stored checkpoints in S3 + manifest files.

2026-03-07: Design review feedback from PM (Ravi): ensure final outputs are deterministic for sampled keys; add dry-run and sample-compare step to pipeline. Action: add a sampling harness and side-by-side comparator.

2026-03-09: Engineering decision: use a hybrid fingerprinting dedupe (event_id + first-100-bytes event payload hash) to handle noisy duplicates and partial reingests. Rationale: balances accuracy with memory footprint.

2026-03-10: Trade-off discussion with infra: Two options for conflict resolution state store — (A) use DynamoDB for per-key latest-write metadata (simpler, higher RPS cost); (B) use RocksDB local state in worker with periodic compaction and checkpoint to S3 (more complex, lower HITS). Decided to prototype option B and fall back to Dynamo if throughput issues arise.

2026-03-11: Implementation update: Delta extractor microservice (Go) implemented with watermark computation and manifest export. Unit tests added. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/replay/pull/419

2026-03-12: Observability: added Prometheus metrics for extracted_delta_size, replayer_apply_rate, conflict_count, and last_successful_checkpoint_timestamp. Grafana dashboard created: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/console-replay/replay-run-ops

2026-03-13: QA run (dry-run) executed on staging using 3-day customer sample. Comparator shows 0.0008% divergences attributable to late tombstone processing; decision: tighten tombstone window and add a reconciliation pass.

2026-03-14: Blocker noted — multi-region ordering issue when replaying across region boundaries. Action: add region-local clocks and causal markers in manifests to preserve per-region order during apply phase. Follow-up subtask to be created.
Follow-ups: create small run to validate RocksDB compaction strategy, add rate limiter to apply workers, prepare release notes and runbook updates before GA
